method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: NOTE ON AXIS: task.json declares axis 'street' (sheets one above the other), but the key maps show both sheets covering the SAME streets (30th-33rd) and different avenues - sheet 63 has L, M, M 1/2, N and sheet 64 has N, N 1/2, O, O 1/2. The seam is therefore vertical and the shared corridor is Avenue N; x is reported, and the axis is recorded as 'avenue'. Evidence: the avenue is labelled 'AVENUE N' at sheet 63's east edge and at sheet 64's west edge. Address runs are exact complements on the one corridor: sheet 63's west frontage reads the even numbers 3004 3006 3008 3010 3012 3014 3016 3018 3020 3022 3024 3026 3028 for the 30th-31st block (past 'STABLE'), then 3102 3104 south of 31st; sheet 64's east frontage reads the odd numbers 3007 3009 3011 3013 3015 3017 3019 3021 3023 3025 3027 for the same block, then 3101 3103. The cross-street run clinches it: 31st St ends ...1420 1422 1424 / 1419 1421 1423 on sheet 63 and resumes 1502 1504 1506 1508 / 1501 1503 1505 1507 on sheet 64, so the 1400/1500 hundred-block break falls on this avenue; the same fire-alarm box ('F.A.' in a pink circle) and T.H. are drawn in the corridor on both plates. One avenue west on sheet 63 is Ave M 1/2 (faces 2078/2289) and one east on sheet 64 is Ave N 1/2 (centre ~1172); neither is shared. Detection's candidates (63: 1749/2937/562; 64: 2056/894/3219) were discarded. Positions are the mid-line of the 70' corridor: sheet 63 faces x=3075 and x=3290 -> 3183; sheet 64 faces x=66 and x=277 -> 172.
